# note.md

> note.md is an agent-ready markdown reader & editor, built for humans and AI agents working in the same plain files. Agents write more than any human can read; the human's job is to read, judge, and keep the few lines only they could have written — the residue no model can generate: judgment, intent, private facts, decisions. Those marks are saved to sidecar `.note.md` files, becoming durable, searchable data that agents read back. Personal Memory follows the same rule: an agent discovers small candidate claims in the work and conversations the user chooses to provide, but only the user can confirm what becomes trusted context. Search finds potentially relevant material; Memory governs the small set of claims an agent may rely on. Because the vault is plain files with shared conventions, it is neutral ground for *many* agents — Cowork, Claude Code, Codex, DeepSeek, ChatGPT, OpenClaw, Hermes — so the human assigns each job to whoever is best and orchestrates them through files; note.md is one client among many. No cloud-owned profile or walled garden: the authority remains in local, Git-tracked files owned by the user.

Linux beta provides .pkg.tar.zst for Omarchy / Arch and .deb for Debian / Ubuntu, each for x86_64 and aarch64. Downloads: https://notemd.net/download?os=linux (choose package format and architecture). Linux and Windows downloads select the latest published release that actually provides the requested package, even when the newest overall release omits it. ARM never falls back to x86_64, and Arch never falls back to Debian packages; unavailable packages lead to the release list. Linux updates use locally downloaded packages and the package manager, outside the desktop updater manifest. The Omarchy repository entry is not yet submitted. Native plugins need a matching Linux build; app-internal agent panels are excluded. Wayland/fcitx5/tray acceptance is pending, and aarch64 has not been verified on a native desktop. Installation and acceptance: https://github.com/wizlijun/note.md/blob/main/docs/linux-omarchy.md.

Key facts: desktop app for macOS 13+ (Apple Silicon & Intel), Windows 10/11 x64, and Linux beta — Tauri, system WebView; distributed macOS builds are signed & notarized. Mobile builds are not published. Platform releases may differ, and some native plugins ship only for macOS; https://notemd.net/download serves each platform its newest available installer. Free to use. The repository uses Apache-2.0; dependencies retain their own licenses, and the current @moraya/core checkout declares PolyForm-Internal-Use-1.0.0. Repo: https://github.com/wizlijun/note.md. The core UI supports English, Chinese, Japanese and German; plugin language coverage varies. note.md includes agent-ready workflows, but it is not an AI model or token provider. These workflows use agents, subscriptions, API accounts, or local runtimes supplied by the user. note.md does not sell token bundles, mark up token prices, or charge a separate per-token fee. Model usage may still consume the user's provider allowance, incur provider API charges, or use local compute. The app itself is developed and maintained using AI coding. Notes are plain files; agents can use the conventions below without this app. Plugin data stores may require their own tools and backups.

## Docs

- [Full product & vault conventions](https://notemd.net/llms-full.txt): everything an agent needs to read or write a note.md vault — sidecar pairing rules, outline format, daily-note paths, wikilink namespace, block citations, CLI (including `notemd search`, the retrieval command).
- [Product homepage](https://notemd.net/): human-facing overview (also in [German](https://notemd.net/de/), [Japanese](https://notemd.net/ja/), and [Chinese](https://notemd.net/zh/)).
- [One vault, many agents](https://notemd.net/orchestrate-agents/): how a human orchestrates Cowork, Codex, ChatGPT, OpenClaw, and Hermes over a single vault, routing each job to the best-fit agent and model.
- [Personal AI memory you confirm](https://notemd.net/blog/personal-ai-memory/): why agents discover candidate memories, humans confirm them one by one, and search remains separate from trusted memory.
- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/wizlijun/note.md): source, releases, README.

## Core conventions (summary)

- `xxx.note.md` beside `xxx.md` = human annotations of that document. `.note.md` without a sibling source = standalone outline note. Never write into a human's `.note.md` unless asked — the one sanctioned exception is the Q&A answer-writeback below.
- Consent-based linking: an agent may *suggest* a `[[link]]`, but only the human confirms what actually connects. Do not auto-link documents or backfill a graph the human didn't ask for.
- Generated knowledge documents use [Open Knowledge Format](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/open-knowledge-format/blob/main/SPEC.md) (OKF) v0.2 metadata, including YAML frontmatter with a `type`. Raw source mirrors, attachments, settings and plugin databases are separate formats. Provenance and trust use `sources`, `generated`, `verified`, `status`, `stale_after` and actor forms `<producer>/<version>`, `human:<id>`, `process:<id>` — never sign your own work `human:`. Preserve unknown fields when editing; do not reject imported documents for missing metadata or broken links. `index.md` / `log.md` are reserved bundle names. See the repository conformance audit for implementation scope.
- `.note.md` body = nested markdown bullet list (an outline), with YAML frontmatter (`type`, `title`, `created`, `updated`).
- Daily notes: `dailynote/{yyyy}/{yyyy-MM-dd}.note.md`; monthly `{yyyy-MM}.note.md`; yearly `{yyyy}.note.md`. Canonical date link: `[[yyyy-MM-dd]]`.
- Wiki notes: `wikipage/{title-slug}.note.md`. Outline links resolve through the vault-wide title index; ordinary Markdown wikilinks resolve relative to the current document.
- Block citation: `((path/to/file.md#b-xxxxxx))` cites one block of a document.
- Multi-agent handoff: several agents may share one vault. They collaborate by passing `.md` files on disk (one agent's output is the next one's input); the human's `.note.md` annotations are the steering signal. Keep the vault in git so every agent write is diffable and revertible.
- Q&A loop: an annotation containing `?` becomes a `type:: question` node
  (`status:: open`) in the companion `.note.md`; agents answer with a
  `type:: answer` child whose body is wrapped in a markdown code fence, and
  set `status:: answered`. The fence must open that bullet (`- ````markdown`)
  — never write `✦` or anything else before it, or the answer is destroyed
  on the next save. The human reads the answer inline under the
  annotated paragraph and may insert it into the document. Only the human
  sets `closed` / `adopted`; agents never edit the main `.md`.
- Notes and Memory revisions are file-backed; search indexes are derived and rebuildable. Health Sync's external SQLite library is durable source data, not a disposable cache, and must be backed up with its attachments.
- Agent playbook: the rules and descriptions that make agents work — `AGENTS.md`, skills, schedules (cron), MCP connections, Memory (`USER.md` / `MEMORY.md`) — are a first-class dataset of the vault, as valuable as its content. The vault copy is the source of truth; copies in a harness's own folders are projections. The root `AGENTS.md` is the entry point and says where the rest lives. You may propose playbook changes, but they take effect only when the human confirms them; never grant yourself new connections, tools, or unattended schedules, and never sign a playbook change `human:`. Keep secrets out of the playbook: store references to credentials, never the credentials. A bad playbook line is executed on every run, so when you propose one, say where it came from; flag conflicts with existing rules instead of overwriting them; put judgment in Markdown rules and skills, and deterministic steps in scripts and schedules.
- Controlled Memory: agents may create pending atomic claims, but cannot create human approval. The user reviews each candidate as confirm, reject, important, or ignore. Approval distinguishes self-representation, factual verification, and behavioral authorization; these meanings never imply one another. Role and scope govern which claims may be recalled or coauthored. Authoritative revisions live under `.notemd/memory/`; readable `USER.md` and `MEMORY.md` are rebuildable projections. Context is selected by space, purpose, consent, time, role, scope, and provider policy rather than similarity alone.
- Retrieval: `notemd search "query" --vault <path>` prints `path:line:text`, one hit per line; `--json` adds `source_ref` (`path#Lline`), `origin` (`human|derived|source|unlabeled`), `provenance` (`agent_by`, `human_verified`) and `attention_minutes` (decayed minutes of the user's own reading/editing attention on that document, 0 = no data — already factored into ranking, exposed so you can explain the order; that data is ingested by the desktop app, the CLI only reads it, so it is 0 everywhere on a machine where the GUI has never opened this vault). A hit with `agent_by` set was written by a model — follow its sources to the primary document rather than citing it as a human's. Exit `1` means no hits, not an error. Default cap is 20 hits — `--all` (or `--limit 0`) returns every hit. `rg`/`grep` remain perfectly valid; this is an accelerator, not a gatekeeper.

## Optional

- Current views and sources: JSON Canvas, table of contents and metadata cards; Timeline, Index Viewer, Knowledge Browser, and Typeset Reader file views; Apple Notes and Roam Research sync, Meetings, Assistant Mail, and Conversation Transcript Corrections. Platform and minimum-host requirements vary by plugin.
- Mermaid code blocks use Pele by default; Graphviz and KaTeX are also supported. Pele syntax differs from Mermaid; switching renderers requires rebuilding, not a settings toggle. See https://github.com/wizlijun/note.md/blob/main/docs/pele-build.md.
- Health Sync (macOS) imports Apple Health files plus Garmin/Oura file and API data into a selected library outside the Vault. NEXT manages tasks and reminder preferences; delivery requires separately configured scripts/services. Quick Launch adds configured apps and CLI commands to the macOS tray with a compatible host. Install and enable plugins separately.
- [CLI](https://github.com/wizlijun/note.md#cli): `notemd` searches the vault, shares documents, writes reports, runs plugin commands, and self-checks the local setup (`notemd doctor` — environment, Vault, search index, plugins, network; `--offline`, `--json`) headlessly.
- Local MCP: `notemd mcp` exposes read-only `search` and `vault_info` tools over stdio. This is separate from the share worker's MCP publishing endpoint. Register it by absolute path with `--cli` (`{"command": "/Applications/note.md.app/Contents/MacOS/notemd", "args": ["--cli", "mcp"]}`); on macOS `notemd mcp setup` prints setup instructions for Claude Code / Claude Desktop / Cowork for the user to paste into Claude Code. Never register it or edit a client's configuration without the user's confirmation.
